reasons.a: Standardisation and the 10-component PCA are fitted once on all 300 rows before the 5-fold CV of the regression; KAP23 sec. 2.4 [L1.2] 'Using the entire dataset for any pre-processing steps such as imputation or over/under sampling' (read online), extended to label-free scaling/PCA by PB sec. 1 O-1; 10 components and 5 folds are the claim's own parameters.
reasons.b: Standardisation, components and regression are all fitted on the training rows of each fold and applied to the test rows (the standard correction); nothing else changes.
reasons.c: The diff is exactly where scores() is called (once on X vs inside each fold); fold seed, regression, pooled R-squared and threshold are identical.
reasons.d: Guards: non-finite values; n < 15 (note's minimum: 11 regression parameters need 12 training rows for one residual df, the PREREG's own convention of 3 pairs for a correlation, and n = 15 is the smallest n whose array_split folds all leave 12 training rows); np.var(y) == 0.0 (MECH_CHECK line 55, zero variance); sd == 0 of a marker (zero variance). The seeded fold permutation inspects nothing. No other branch on the input.
reasons.e: No banned PB sec. 4 term in claim, keys or meanings (scripted check by the auditor too); the brief does not say what 'claim false' means.
reasons.f: Source states no sizes (KAP23 [L1.2] entry); 300 patients x 80 markers (24 000 values) is of the order of a clinical biomarker-panel cohort as the note argues, within 1000 per axis and 500 000 values; listed as 'sizes not documented by the source'.
reasons.g: Same statistic (pooled out-of-fold R-squared), threshold 0.15, decision rule and code; the faulty does one SVD instead of five (same order of cost, milliseconds).
reasons.h: Brief states sizes, axes (patients, markers), what each key measured, and the claim; 'first 10 principal components' and '5-fold cross-validation' are allowed by the estimand line; no statement about how rows are arranged, shared or selected; no key named by a role.
reasons.i: Claim = predictive R-squared for new patients of the PCA-regression pipeline estimated by 5-fold CV, which is what the fixed criterion estimates (estimand line of CASE.md and PRIVATE.json).

reasons.a: Children whose severity rating lies strictly between the 35th and 65th percentile are dropped before the CV, so intermediate cases are never evaluated; KAP23 sec. 2.4 [L3.3] (Bone et al.): excluding borderline cases means 'the test set is no longer representative of the general population about which claims are made' (read online). KAP23 gives no band width; the 30 percent band is the note's declared choice.
reasons.b: The same stratified 5-fold logistic pipeline on all children (borderline ones included); nothing else changes.
reasons.c: The diff is the keep line plus reading the rating and its finiteness check, which only the faulty needs; folds, Newton steps, ridge, balanced accuracy and threshold are identical.
reasons.d: Guards: non-finite values; n < 10 or fewer than 2 per diagnosis value (MECH_CHECK line 70/68: 2 per class is the smallest count that puts both classes in every training fold, and 10 is below the size at which an unpenalised logistic fit on 30 measures is non-degenerate, about 32 training rows); X.std == 0 (MECH_CHECK line 72/70, zero variance). The percentile band is the error itself, not a probe test; on all-zero ratings it keeps every row.
reasons.e: No banned term; no negation of the claim.
reasons.f: Source states no sizes (KAP23 [L3.3] and the Bone et al. example as read); 400 children x 30 measures is of the order of a clinic cohort as the note argues, within the caps; listed as 'sizes not documented by the source'.
reasons.g: Same statistic (pooled balanced accuracy), threshold 0.70, rule and cost (the faulty fits on about 70 percent of the rows).
reasons.h: Keys are named by what they measured ('clinician's overall symptom severity rating ... 0 to 10 scale, higher means more severe' describes the measurement and its scale); no fact about how rows are related, ordered or selected; the claim names the referred population, which the estimand line requires; no key named by its role in the error.
reasons.i: Claim = balanced accuracy for new referred children (whole population), which the fixed criterion estimates on all children.

reasons.a: Three equal-variance t tests (liking, willingness to pay, their average) and 'holds' if any is significant with a positive difference; SIM11 Table 1 note: 'three t tests, one on each of two dependent variables and a third on the average of these two variables' (read online), 20 per cell, alpha .05. The raw average follows the source's wording.
reasons.b: The single test on the one measure the claim names (pre-specified outcome), same test and alpha; nothing else changes.
reasons.c: The diff is the list of comparisons (three vs one) and reading the two willingness-to-pay keys; the test, p-value helper, direction and loop are identical.
reasons.d: Guards: non-finite values; fewer than 2 per condition (smallest size for a two-sample t); pooled variance == 0 (zero variance). MECH_CHECK lists nothing. No other branch on the input.
reasons.e: No banned term; no negation of the claim.
reasons.f: Source size used: 20 per cell (SIM11 Table 1 baseline); within the caps.
reasons.g: Same statistic, test, threshold, direction and 'any over a list' rule; cost 3 tests vs 1, microseconds.
reasons.h: Keys name what each measured (liking, willingness to pay, per condition); the claim names only liking; no statement about how participants or variables are related, ordered or selected; no key named by its role.
reasons.i: Claim = treatment-minus-control difference in mean liking by a pooled t test, which is exactly the fixed criterion.

reasons.a: A t test at n = 10, 11, ..., 50 per condition (first n of each array) and 'holds' if any look is significant with a positive difference; SIM11 Figure 1 text: start at 10, test after every new per-condition observation, stop at significance or 50, 22 percent (read online).
reasons.b: One test on all 50 per condition (the fixed-n analysis); nothing else changes.
reasons.c: The diff is the list of sizes (10..50 vs [n_max]); test, helper, direction and loop are identical.
reasons.d: Guards: non-finite values; fewer than 2 per condition; pooled variance == 0 at a look (zero variance). min(10, n_max) only shortens the look list for arrays shorter than 10, never on the declared shapes. MECH_CHECK lists nothing.
reasons.e: No banned term; no negation of the claim.
reasons.f: Source sizes used: maximum 50 per condition, first look at 10 (SIM11 Figure 1).
reasons.g: Same statistic, test, threshold and rule; 41 tests vs 1, microseconds.
reasons.h: Keys name the score per condition; 'on all participants' is part of the claim and allowed by the estimand line; the brief does not state recruitment order or any other arrangement of the rows.
reasons.i: Claim = mean difference at the full size by a pooled t test, which is exactly the fixed criterion (fixed uses min of the two lengths, equal to all 50 under the brief).

reasons.a: np.roll(mask, 1) makes each listed probe set's row be replaced by the adjacent row; BAG09 sec. 3.2 'a single row shift: ... quantifications from row 98 ... were used instead of those from row 97' and sec. 3.9 'an off-by-one indexing error affecting all genes reported' (read online); shift of one row as documented.
reasons.b: The membership mask as given; nothing else changes.
reasons.c: The diff is the single np.roll line (plus its comment).
reasons.d: Guards: non-finite expression; fewer than 1 listed probe set or fewer than 2 per sensitivity group (Welch defined); v1 + v2 == 0 (zero variance). MECH_CHECK's abs(delta - 1.0) < 1e-15 is the convergence tolerance of the incomplete-beta continued fraction, a numerical constant, not a test of the input.
reasons.e: No banned term ('False if resistant' in a key meaning is a dtype description, not a negation of the claim).
reasons.f: Probe-set axis reduced to the cap (source arrays 12 558 to 22 283 probe sets, PRIVATE.json, BAG09); 60 cell lines = the NCI-60 panel the source uses; 60 000 values; listed as 'reduced to the cap'.
reasons.g: Same statistic (Welch on per-line signature averages), thresholds 0.5 and .01, rule and cost.
reasons.h: Keys name what they hold (expression, membership of the published list, sensitivity class); the claim names the signature, as the estimand line requires; no statement about how probe sets or lines are ordered or selected; 'on_signature' is not a role in the error (the error is the misalignment).
reasons.i: Claim = sensitive-minus-resistant difference in the mean expression of the signature's own probe sets, which the fixed criterion estimates.

reasons.a: The averaging range leaves out five of the 20 country rows; HER14 (PERI WP322 version, read online): the spreadsheet error 'entirely excludes five countries ... from the analysis', footnote 'RR averaged cells in lines 30 to 44 instead of lines 30 to 49'. The code drops the last five rows, the note's text says 'first five' as well; the skeleton's country rows are exchangeable, so the readings are equivalent (logged by the author).
reasons.b: Both means over all 20 countries' country-years; nothing else changes (both twins use country-year weighting, as the claim's wording defines; RR's country weighting is not part of either twin).
reasons.c: The diff is the row range (growth[:15] vs all).
reasons.d: Guards: non-finite values; an empty debt group (fewer than 1 country-year above or at-or-below 90; a difference of means is defined from one value each). Under the noise and zeros probes no value exceeds 90, so both twins abstain: an allowed empty-selection guard caused by the claim's 90 boundary, identical in both twins.
reasons.e: No banned term; no negation of the claim.
reasons.f: Source sizes used exactly: 20 advanced economies, 1946 to 2009 (64 years), 1280 values.
reasons.g: Same statistic (difference of pooled means), threshold -2 points, rule and cost.
reasons.h: Keys name growth and debt ratio by country and year; the claim names the 90 percent boundary and growth, as the estimand line requires; no statement about country order or selection.
reasons.i: Claim = difference in mean growth between high-debt and other country-years across the 20 economies, which the fixed criterion estimates.
